key_insight: QuantiSpect replaces dense 3D convolutions with structure-aware factorized branches to keep surface-code decoding accurate while dramatically cutting model size and compute.
engineering_relevance: This makes real-time quantum error correction more practical by lowering decoder latency and resource cost for scalable fault-tolerant quantum hardware.
method: Uses a lightweight 3D CNN pre-decoder for the rotated surface code.
Replaces each dense residual block with depthwise spatial, depthwise temporal, and grouped spatio-temporal branches.
Adds squeeze-and-excitation channel gating to fuse branch outputs and exploit syndrome structure.
evidence_signal: On a 4×A100 benchmark, the R=13 model matched the Accurate baseline’s receptive field with 0.663M vs 1.80M parameters and about 2.84× fewer per-voxel MACs, while the expanded R=21 variant improved threshold to about 0.80% and further reduced logical error rates.
watch_item: The approach is benchmarked on specific code distances and hardware assumptions, so deployment still needs validation for different noise models, decoder stacks, and system-level latency constraints.
paper_title: QuantiSpect: A Structure-Aware Lightweight 3D CNN Pre-Decoder for Scalable Surface Code Quantum Error Correction
